context: Coerce at the boundary where the value enters the adapter, not at the point of use, so every consumer of self.thread_limit sees a real int: in __init__, `int()` the value and raise a clear ValueError naming the option when it is not integral. For the two string settings, prefer DuckDB's parameterised SET where the version in use supports it; where it does not, validate against the same bounded memory-size pattern MCP already applies (benchbox/mcp/schemas.py MEMORY_LIMIT_PATTERN) before interpolating, rather than escaping quotes. Add a test that a non-integral thread_limit is rejected at construction and never reaches conn.execute -- assert on a connection spy, because asserting only on the raised error would pass even if the statement had already been sent.
description:
benchbox/platforms/duckdb.py:667 reads `self.thread_limit = config.get("thread_limit")` with no type coercion, and :800 applies it as `conn.execute(f"SET threads TO {self.thread_limit}")` -- raw interpolation of a config-supplied value into SQL.

This is a consequence of my own change. Before #1514, DuckDBAdapter.from_config omitted `thread_limit` from its pass-through key list, so the only way to reach :800 was to call the constructor directly. Adding `thread_limit` to that list (which is what made MCP's duckdb.threads actually apply) also connected the unified-config and config-file paths to the interpolation.

Not an MCP escalation: MCP_PLATFORM_OPTION_ALLOWLIST bounds duckdb.threads to an int in 1..256 and _prepare_adapter_platform_options renames it, so nothing string-shaped survives that boundary. The exposure is the non-MCP path -- a benchmark config or profile YAML carrying `thread_limit: "4; ATTACH 'x' AS y"` is interpolated verbatim. Config files are comparatively trusted, hence medium rather than high, but the surface was widened without being noticed at review time and should not stay that way.

Note :790 `SET memory_limit = '{self.memory_limit}'` and :795 max_temp_directory_size have the same shape and were already live before #1514; fix them in the same pass rather than leaving a half-hardened file. See [duckdb-from-config-drops-constructor-read-keys], which covers the adjacent question of which other constructor-read keys from_config still drops.

Identified 2026-08-04 during the adversarial review of the mcp-v2-platform-options batch.

preserves.behavior: An absent thread_limit still means 'do not emit SET threads at all', not 'emit a default'
MCP duckdb.threads keeps reaching the effective DuckDB `SET threads` statement -- the TestMCPThreadsReachTheEffectiveSetting coverage added by #1514 must still pass

verifications.description: A non-integral thread_limit never reaches conn.execute
verifications.expected: exits 0 with a new case proving construction fails and the connection spy recorded no SET statement

verifications.description: The MCP path still applies the requested thread count end to end
